studies.Title: Effects of soy protein isolate consumption on prostate cancer biomarkers in men with HGPIN, ASAP, and low-grade prostate cancer.
studies.Reference: Effects of soy protein isolate consumption on prostate cancer biomarkers in men with HGPIN, ASAP, and low-grade prostate cancer.
studies.Population: men at high risk of prostate cancer or with low-grade prostate cancer
studies.comparison_type: soy protein groups versus milk protein isolate group

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Fifty-eight men at high risk of prostate cancer or with low-grade prostate cancer were randomly assigned to consume 1 of 3 protein isolates containing 40 g protein: 1) soy protein (SPI+, 107 mg isoflavones/d); 2) alcohol-washed soy protein (SPI-, <6 mg isoflavones/d); or 3) milk protein (MPI).
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: a lower rate of prostate cancer developed in the soy groups compared to the milk group (P = 0.01)
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: a lower rate of prostate cancer developed in the soy groups compared to the milk group
extraction_supporting_text.design: were randomly assigned to consume 1 of 3 protein isolates
extraction_supporting_text.timing: less prostate cancer is detected after 6 mo of soy consumption
